cefrAlignment: Matches B2 listening (CEFR CV: can follow detailed directions and extended talk on familiar topics at normal speed): the 200–300-word monologues use dense location language (diagonally opposite, beyond, at the far end) and need the listener to track a moving route while changing direction.
examFidelity: Mirrors IELTS Listening Part 2 map/plan labelling: lettered maps with two spare letters, places asked in audio order, and a distractor named next to each target; I checked every answer against the SVG coordinates (park: A visitor centre, B toilets, H picnic area, D playground, E bird hide, G café; arts centre: B, D, A, E, G, C, with F and H unused) and all are correct and unambiguous.
fixes: Dictation: replaced 'The café is directly opposite the box office.' with 'The workshop is directly opposite the staff office.' The dictation checker removes non-ASCII letters, so a learner typing 'cafe' was marked wrong. The new sentence also matches the plan (C is opposite H).
Softened the unverified '30 seconds' of preparation time, in the learn text and the IELTS exam tip, to 'the time you are given before Part 2'.
Model walkthrough: replaced 'Real tests usually have one or two extra letters' with the more accurate 'exam maps usually have more letters than questions'.
openConcerns: Code-level, outside this file: words() in src/lib/utils.ts strips accented letters, so any dictation sentence with é or similar letters marks plain-ASCII typing as wrong. The same café/cafe mismatch would affect gap answers.
TTS: the Woman/Man phone call may get voices that do not match the speaker labels. Nothing in the test depends on gender, but a specialist should listen to check naturalness.
learnerOutcome: A learner who completes the lesson can orient themselves on a map or floor plan, convert left/right into compass directions while the speaker changes direction, and label 6 places correctly while ignoring nearby distractors.
